description: I am a 17 yr old studying in dubai and i am a very curious person imo, i really wanted to bring my maybe helpful ideas to life in a very fun and interactive way.
summary:
MarsBound VR is a Mars exploration simulator created by Ansha Javeed and Arjun Brar, both high school students, for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Dubai.

Inspired by NASA’s challenge of helping future astronauts explore Mars safely and efficiently, we wanted to create a platform that brings different types of Martian data together in one place.

Using real NASA data, MarsBound allows users to explore the Martian surface, discover important locations, drive rovers, fly drones and experience the planet through VR. It also includes environmental monitoring, soil experiments and underground greenhouse simulations to help users understand the challenges of exploring and potentially living on Mars. Our project can also be used on web incase a VR experience isnt not available, this way our app is suitable for all.

We have also included six languages and different learning modes to make the platform accessible to more people.

We wanted to make this experience useful not only for students but also for understanding how future Mars exploration could work.

Our goal is to turn NASA’s discoveries into an interactive experience that brings us one step closer to understanding the Red Planet.
details: MarsBound is an interactive Mars exploration simulator designed to make real NASA data easier to explore and understand. We used Claude AI to assist in developing the application, along with Python, JavaScript and WebXR. The platform recreates Martian terrain using NASA datasets and allows users to explore Mars, monitor environmental conditions and conduct virtual experiments. It aims to make space science more accessible and inspire future explorers. What makes our project creative is its combination of real scientific data, VR and interactive learning. We also included six languages: English, Arabic, Hindi, Spanish, French and Chinese, to reach a wider international audience and make Mars exploration accessible across different cultures. Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, user experience and the needs of future astronauts.
